title: Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem and the Horace method (Brambilla–Ottaviani), via Emsalem–Iarrobino apolarity
text: By apolarity, degree-3 maximal rank of the selector conditions D_l^2 w = 0 on the matching complex K_3 is a matching-complex analogue of Alexander–Hirschowitz independence of generic double points on cubics. Translate the Horace degeneration: specialize some forms to vanish on one row and run the residual exact sequence relating K_3 of the board to K_3 and K_2 of the board without that row, inducting on n up to the capacity min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)).
reason: Developed into row Horace and the pattern-algebra reduction, which stop at the open coupling (C); the capacity-sharp all-n form and higher degrees remain. The idea was carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-27-equivalence-route-review:3 and entry-2026-09-28-ideal-sum-review:1 (dedupe against them).

title: Artinian reduction of the chessboard complex's face ring and Hochster's formula (with chessboard connectivity and Shareshian–Wachs torsion)
text: If the top algebra G (or a squarefree Gröbner degeneration of it) is an Artinian reduction of a face ring of a chessboard-type complex, Hochster's formula turns Tor vanishing for wide monomial tops into homology vanishing of induced chessboard subcomplexes, where chessboard connectivity and Shareshian–Wachs torsion apply. This targets the width axis (A2) and Tor vanishing for wide tops.
reason: Partly developed: the observations entry found Hochster's Tor is a different Tor, and the Gröbner-degeneration entry produced a squarefree complex Delta' for degree 3 only; no wide-top Tor statement followed. Carried later as standard item entry-2026-09-27-designed-line-review:1 (dedupe).

title: Lefschetz theorems for Artinian reductions of face rings and the anisotropy method (Adiprasito; Papadakis–Petrotou, odd characteristic)
text: Maximal-rank multiplication by squares of forms on G is a Lefschetz-type property; characteristic-p anisotropy gives Lefschetz elements for generic Artinian reductions of face rings of spheres, pseudomanifolds and cycles. A characteristic-3 version adapted to the Frobenius syzygies (l^3 = 0) would supply Tor vanishing in degree for clause tops.
reason: Carried in entry-2026-09-25-outside-leads-review and tested in entry-2026-09-27-moment-route-review, which falsified it as a route to the F_3-random statement (generic over a transcendental extension; power-form Lefschetz fails since elements cube to zero). Whether a designed or explicit F_3 use remains is not settled.

title: Gröbner and torus degenerations with upper semicontinuity of Tor (the method of the known cases of Fröberg's conjecture)
text: Degenerate the algebra G (not the forms) to a monomial or torus-fixed fiber where Taylor resolutions compute Tor, prove vanishing or maximal rank there, and lift it back by semicontinuity. Targets Tor vanishing through degree 22k (A3) and row freeness.
reason: Positive at degree 3 (lem:degeneration-transfer), refuted for row freeness because the torus rescales the row sums (degeneration-row-freeness), and falsified for monomial row sums under one order only ("other orders were not searched"). Explicit F_3-rational specializations at higher degree remain untried. Related standard items: fall-tolerance-review:3, row-free-line-review.

title: Representation stability for FI-modules (Church–Ellenberg–Farb) for the n to infinity axis
text: The map from n to K_t(n) is a functor on injections adding rows and labels; Noetherianity turns vanishing up to the generation degree into vanishing for all n. A fixed tuple of forms breaks the symmetry, so it needs equivariant configurations (orbit specializations) with M growing with n, or symmetry in law as for W_RS random families.
reason: Used successfully for the base (thm:tensor-power-freeness via Church–Ellenberg); for forms, falsified for adversarial coefficients (coupling-free review) and left "Not run" for the W_RS failure space, which is symmetric only in expectation (capacity review). The equivariant-family version was never attempted.

title: Čech and Leray vanishing on the member cover
text: The gluing obstruction is a first Čech group on the cover of the inventory by its members, identified with Tor; a Leray-type theorem would make it vanish when the cover is good, with higher obstructions vanishing on overlaps. Candidate proof strategy for local falls on adversarial families (pencils are bad overlaps).
reason: Developed in the cover-gluing entries of 27 September but carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-26-fall-tolerance-review:2 and entry-2026-09-28-satisfiable-cover-review:1, whose audits govern it (dedupe).

title: Modular representation theory of (Z/3)^M: Dade's lemma, rank and support varieties, Jordan types
text: A = F_3[x_1..x_M]/(x_j^3) is the group algebra of (Z/3)^M with x_j = g_j - 1, so G is a representation with each generator acting as 1 + l_j, and Tor vanishing is truncated relative projectivity. Rank/support varieties and Jordan types could certify it beyond single generic elements.
reason: Heavily developed later (truncated and graded Dade, Jordan-type entries) and carried as standard items entry-2026-09-25-closure-route-review:1, entry-2026-09-27-directness-route-review:1, entry-2026-09-27-local-independence-review:3 and entry-2026-09-28-coupled-cover-review:2 (dedupe).

title: Fröberg's conjecture: semi-regularity of squares of generic forms in G
text: Tor vanishing through B means G/(l_j^2) has its expected Hilbert function through B, a Fröberg-type semi-regularity statement on the injective side, far below capacity. Proofs of the known cases (specialization plus openness, witness families) are the template for A3.
reason: Carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-27-survival-review:1 and entry-2026-09-27-convergence-review:2 (dedupe); A3 remains open at logarithmic degree.

title: Tropical leading weights with ties (extending lem:tropical-leading-bound)
text: Assign tropical weights to cells so that the leading matrix of the double-point map is computable; tie-free weights cap at M(gamma_1-2), so use weights with ties and a second-order leading matrix to reach min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) on the pattern algebra for every n.
reason: Developed into thm:tetrahedral-double-points (about n^3/1330 explicit selectors at degree 3, every n); the capacity-sharp form is paused at the coupling, and whether tied weights extend beyond degree 3 or to wide tops was not tried.

title: Gale duality for the column model (squares of Gale-dual linear forms)
text: Freeness of a column span in the column model equals the Hilbert function of Sym(V)/(m_1^2..m_n^2) with m_j the Gale transform of the hole-value configuration, a Fröberg/Alexander–Hirschowitz question for a specific point configuration. Locate the special position of the Gale points in the defective degree-4 and degree-5 configurations to decide column freeness.
reason: Partly developed (frobenius-class-apolarity handles the characteristic-3 apolarity), but the proposed special-position analysis of defective Gale configurations was not found later; column freeness at density one half is still conjectured in W.

title: Razborov's PC degree lower bound for PHP and its description of the PHP ideal, for base stability (a)
text: Read Razborov's analysis to prove that weak unary PHP alone has no fall below logarithmic degree, hypothesis (a) of relative gluing.
reason: Hypothesis (a) was settled at logarithmic degree (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic, tensor-power freeness), so the lead has no remaining target.

title: Constant Jordan type theory (Carlson–Friedlander–Pevtsova) for truncated freeness of tensor powers
text: Modules whose restrictions to all lines have the same Jordan type; their generic-kernel or tensor-product results might give truncated freeness for tensor powers of u(W)/m^2, the if-half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness.
reason: Superseded: thm:tensor-power-freeness proved the conjecture at p = 3 by peeling and FI-modules. Jordan-type ideas for other targets are carried by later standard items.

title: Family-dependent substitution in the style of the Weak Rank Principle (Garlík, Gryaznov, Ren, Tzameret, arXiv 2608.08760)
text: Find a substitution, depending on the family, that sends each W clause (1-L_i^2) prod L_j^2 into the PHP ideal at logarithmic degree, as Y := X^T A sends rank constraints into degree-2 consequences of functional PHP before Razborov's bound applies.
reason: Developed (dense-axiom literature, composition collapse, weak-rank selectors, base selectors) and carried as standard item entry-2026-09-26-thread-review-4:3, whose audit governs (dedupe); base selectors left a corollary with expensive selectors not pushed to a bound.

title: Pseudo-calibration for many random dense constraints (Ghosh, Jeronimo, Jones, Potechin, Rajendran, arXiv 2009.01874)
text: Build pseudo-expectations or designs by matching low-degree moments of a planted distribution, as done for SoS with polynomially many random dense constraints. Here the target is a Nullstellensatz design on the allowed set for random-prefix families.
reason: Dismissed in the review by a one-step objection (adversarial forms break it); later reviews raised it repeatedly and it is carried as standard item entry-2026-09-28-certificate-halves-review:1 (dedupe).

title: Symmetric-system lower-bound methods (Potechin–Grigoriev; Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret functional lower bounds)
text: These methods prove degree lower bounds by exploiting the symmetry of the whole system. W_RS families are invariant in law under permutations of pigeons and holes, so a symmetrized design (averaging a candidate over the group action) or an expected-case version might apply to random-prefix families even though a fixed adversarial family is not symmetric.
reason: Closed only by the one-step objection that an adversarial family breaks symmetry; no entry tried the symmetry-in-law version for W_RS.

title: Closure of linear forms (Efremenko–Itsykson amortized closure; Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson; Bhattacharya–Chattopadhyay; Byramji–Impagliazzo)
text: Closure operators handle dense linear forms natively for regular or bounded-depth Res(+). An F_3 analogue for regular or bounded-depth Res(Lin_F3) on PHP plus dense blocks would be an intermediate target and a possible batched mechanism.
reason: Read in the source later (ordered closure: not span-invariant over F_3; parity literature); the closure sub-line is parked as weak, but whether a regular-fragment version at odd p was attempted is unclear.

title: Part's subset-sum bounds in Res(lin_F_q) via code distance (arXiv 2202.08214)
text: Dense linear inputs handled through code distance, for characteristic at least 5 and a restricted fragment.
reason: The Boolean-linear entry read the source and found it covers a weak regular fragment splitting on variables, for linear systems not PHP, and W_RS clauses are subspace avoidances, not linear systems.

title: Wilson's mod-p inclusion-matrix rank theorem, in a several-form version
text: Column Wilson gives Taylor generation for one sparse clause at every degree; a mod-p rank theorem for several set systems at once would give Taylor generation for many clause tops, including the Koszul range and overlapping supports.
reason: Taken as the main line: several-form Wilson, column-disjoint Taylor, bounded clusters and conj:two-form-wilson-taylor; designed families are settled, while the block-line review found no local-to-global principle for many forms. It now lives as route conjectures rather than a lead.
